title: CoT Faithfulness Variation by Task Type: Math vs. Factual vs. Ethical vs. Commonsense
original_idea: Replicate the Anthropic CoT faithfulness methodology (hint injection, post-hoc rationalization detection) across four task types. Measure unfaithfulness rate by category.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The task-type variation in CoT faithfulness has been documented across multiple recent papers (FaithCoT-Bench, Counterfactual Simulation Training). Replicating with the same four task types adds limited new insight.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Hint injection methodology requires careful experimental design. Four task types multiply the work. Moderately accessible but requires understanding of the methodology.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Four task types each requiring scenario design, data collection, and analysis is too broad for 30hrs. Would need to reduce to 2 task types to be feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Anthropic's 'Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think' (arxiv 2505.05410) tested CoT faithfulness across six hint categories including sycophancy, consistency, and metadata cues. FaithCoT-Bench (arxiv 2510.04040) provides a unified benchmark with 1,000+ trajectories across four domains. 'Counterfactual Simulation Training for CoT Faithfulness' (arxiv 2602.20710) explicitly showed that process/skill-based tasks (like SNLI) are more amenable to faithfulness improvements than knowledge-intensive tasks (MMLU-Pro-Law, ETHICS-commonsense). The core finding that CoT faithfulness varies by task type and that knowledge-intensive vs. reasoning tasks differ substantially has been established across multiple 2025-2026 papers.
